title: Per-customer Eval Suites with Privacy Guards for Dedicated & Private
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem statement: Customers running Redwood Dedicated or Private want regression monitoring that reflects their real workloads and SLAs, without exposing sensitive data to Redwood-hosted eval pipelines. Current global eval suites are useful for platform-level regressions but fail to capture tenant-specific prompt distributions, domain vocabulary, and safety constraints. Goal: deliver per-customer eval suites and a privacy-first execution model so we can gate model/config changes using customer-representative metrics while preserving data isolation and compliance requirements.

Scope: define configuration model for customer eval suites, add a private execution mode for evals that can run inside customer VPCs or on-prem runners, integrate results into Console with alerting and regression gating, and provide a safe path for customers to submit testcases (PII handling, redaction/templating). Not in scope: building a fully managed per-customer data labeling service.

Success metrics: 1) First 5 enterprise customers adopt customer evals in dedicated/private mode within 8 weeks of GA. 2) Regression gate prevents at least two rollout incidents in the quarter. 3) <0.1% risk of sensitive data leaving customer network (audited).

Non-functional constraints: must support air-gapped envs, KMS/HSM keying for result encryption, and role-based access controls so only customer admins and authorized Redwood SEs can view raw testcases.

Proposed approach: 1) Configuration: allow customers to upload a named eval suite (JSONL) with optional metadata tags and sensitivity level labels. 2) Execution modes: hosted-simulated (for non-sensitive suites), private-exec (runner image + small orchestration that runs inside customer VPC/on-prem and pushes only aggregated metrics back). 3) Privacy controls: data sanitization helpers (templating, automated PII scanner with redaction options), result encryption with customer-managed KMS, opt-in telemetry. 4) Integration: results flow into Console per-route/model dashboard with trend charts, regression alerts, and a gating API that ties to rollout policies (canary/block). 5) Developer UX: CLI and Console UIs for uploading suites, running adhoc, and scheduling nightly evaluations.

Key stakeholders: PM (Aisha), Eng owners (Liam Chen - Eval infra, Maria Gomez - Security), Design (Theo Park), Solutions/SE for pilot customers (Jordan Rivera).

Open questions: - What minimal telemetry must be returned from private-exec to allow platform monitoring without leaking prompts? - How will we price/rate-limit private execution runs for Dedicated? - What are the legal boundaries for storing customer-provided testcases? Need legal input.

Artifacts: planning doc https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/QG/pages/Customer+Eval+Suites, proto UI mock in Figma https://www.figma.com/file/abc123/customer-evals, initial GH spike PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/evals/pull/153
acceptance_criteria: Customers can register an eval suite (JSONL) in Console or via CLI
Private-exec runner image is published and can be deployed into customer VPCs with documented installation steps
Only aggregated metrics (percentages, histograms) are transmitted to Redwood by default; raw testcases remain in customer network unless explicitly permitted
Console shows per-customer eval trend charts and attaches to rollout policies as a gating signal
Security review completed and encryption/KMS flows documented
Pilot with 2 enterprise customers completed and feedback incorporated
tasks: Define eval suite schema and sensitivity labels (PM/Eng)
Design Console UI for suite upload, run, and trends
Implement metrics-only reporting pipeline with encryption and auth
Create CLI commands for uploading/scheduling runs
Write security and compliance runbook and complete legal review
Pilot + iterate with Solutions/SE on 2 customers
